Thanks — three quick items from legal's side before we get counterparty redlines: 

1) Data residency / exhibit on data handling: Elena, can you confirm whether Brightsea requires EU residency or any special processing restrictions? If so, we'll pull the EU exhibit and flag additional security controls.

2) SLA/backstop: we'll propose a 99.9% uptime SLA in the MSA but include our standard fallback policy. If Brightsea has stricter SLA needs, flag now so we can check feasibility with infra.

3) IP / derivative works: if Brightsea wants a narrow usage license vs. assignment of outputs, note that in Exhibit C.

Marissa — I'll prepare a one-page summary of our proposed redline positions and a suggested negotiation matrix so sales can track concessions. Karthik, once Elena confirms PO/net-45, can you confirm the billing contact and whether we should create net-45 terms in our billing system or route invoices through procurement@brightsea.com?

- SLA: 99.9% is acceptable; we'll flag any material exceptions after initial trial.
- IP: Brightsea prefers a license limited to internal product use (no assignment). Counsel will propose language to reflect that.
- Procurement: confirmed — we'll issue a PO with net-45 terms to procurement@redwood.ai. Accounting will copy finance@brightsea.com.
